data.recommendation: Adopt one converged, implementable plan with four deliverables. (1) UNCONDITIONAL — additive generalized builder tools/build_cuda.py (codex's name adopted); tools/build_gb10.py, requirements/gb10.txt, the verified upstream checkout, and all audited evidence stay byte-identical. The builder adds a standard-library preflight (venv, toolkit, nvcc-target support, GPU detection), replaces upstream gencode flags only in disposable source copies via the same preimage-hash patch discipline (SETUP_HASHES pattern in build_gb10.py), suppresses installation after failed preflight, and records toolchain versions, source/patch hashes, commands, failures, and the ACTUAL extension gencode flags (not torch.cuda.get_arch_list(), which only describes Torch's own targets). Initial scope: Linux x86_64 + aarch64 on the pinned software profile; broad Torch/CUDA matrices deferred. Acceptance gate on the available GB10: successful rebuild of sm121, existing numerical forward/backward parity checks (check_gpu_runtime.py structure) pass against the newly built extensions, and a bounded smoke of the ORIGINAL configured model — finite loss and gradients, an optimizer update, checkpoint reload, valid native inference — labeled a functional smoke, not a benchmark. Per-hardware promotion rule: any other Linux NVIDIA configuration is 'expected-to-build, unverified' until the same checks pass on that hardware. (2) EVIDENCE-GATED — CPU reference execution tier. Ordinary-session implementation is authorized, so the go/no-go is executed against actual sources during implementation: inspect mamba_simple.py, predict.py, and upstream setup.py; IF the pinned configured model (including the bimamba branch it actually uses, or a documented explicit exclusion) can be driven through a separate vendored, hash-pinned module of the pure-Torch reference math (selective_scan_ref, causal_conv1d_ref, plain-Torch RMSNorm) plus a new CPU entry point, with zero edits to pinned upstream Python sources, THEN ship it; ELSE descope to a documented subset or defer, recording the blocking file as the anchor in the support matrix. If shipped, acceptance is MODEL-LEVEL equivalence on GB10, not operator parity alone: same configured model and checkpoint/parameter structure, FP32 outputs, input and parameter gradients within tolerances, checkpoint reload followed by inference, with bounded batch size and steps. CPU tier is FP32-only with autocast explicitly disabled (adopting codex's correction: torch.autocast('cpu') defaults to bfloat16 and is not an FP32 substitute); fp16 claims remain CUDA-only. Only after the GB10 model-level gate passes does hosted-runner CI run a tiny synthetic-data CPU train/infer smoke on Linux/Windows/macOS (no raw data or weights). (3) CI + FAILURE PATHS — extend the existing ci.yml to a Linux/Windows/macOS × Python 3.10/3.12 matrix with portable invocations; fix or precisely scope any filesystem/subprocess assumptions the new OSes surface. Substantive failure-path tests with temp dirs and controlled subprocess fixtures: wrong machine/venv/Torch parser.error exits, patch preimage-hash mismatch aborts, unsafe build directories, build-process failure with retained failure reports, no installation after failed preflight, installed-source mismatch, and (if the CPU tier ships) clean diagnostic failure when CUDA-only features are requested and loud failure if the vendored reference no longer hash-matches upstream. (4) SUPPORT MATRIX — docs/support-matrix.md with per-row evidence levels: GB10 measured (three 120-epoch runs preserved untouched); other Linux NVIDIA expected-to-build/unverified pending the promotion rule; CPU/Windows/macOS scoped to exactly what ran (tooling + offline evidence, plus CPU model execution only if the gate passed); containers deferred as a non-load-bearing convenience at most. Hosted workflow results describe only the operations actually executed on each recorded runner. Bounded to reproducibility/portability; no IDS/NPU, no data/weights redistribution, ESCALATED video-quality review untouched.

codex blocker 2 (operator parity insufficient; need model-level preservation): resolved by adopting model-level equivalence as the CPU-tier acceptance gate — same configured model, matching parameter/checkpoint structure, FP32 outputs, input and parameter gradients, checkpoint reload plus inference, bounded batch/steps — before any CI claim.

my blocker 1 (codex route verifies zero new execution on other systems): resolved because the converged artifact retains CPU reference execution as a gated deliverable with a defined decision rule and hosted-runner verification path, rather than an open-ended deferral; if the gate fails, the limitation is anchored and documented, which is a defensible discharge of the requirement.

data.recommendation:
Converge on a staged hybrid, with CPU delivery contingent on source review. A generalized CUDA builder is the smallest code change, but GB10 verification establishes no additional hardware configuration. A CPU reference backend could establish actual execution on hosted systems, provided the complete configured model imports and executes correctly. Container-only distribution retains CPU architecture, GPU and driver constraints; defer it.

Preserve the pinned scientific sources, build_gb10.py, requirements/gb10.txt and historical evidence. Add tools/build_cuda.py with a bounded, pinned Linux software profile, selected-device and compiler-target checks, disposable source copies, hash-guarded compatibility patches, and reports recording actual extension flags, provenance and failures. Require a fresh GB10 rebuild, numerical forward/backward checks and a bounded original-model training/inference smoke with finite gradients, an optimizer update and checkpoint reload.

For CPU, establish the complete import and dispatch design before committing to delivery. If feasible without editing pinned scientific sources, add an explicit FP32 reference backend and entry point preserving the configured architecture, preprocessing and checkpoint structure. Disable autocast. Acceptance must compare the complete configured model against native CUDA FP32 using identical weights, controlled stochastic behavior and predefined tolerances for outputs, differentiable inputs and parameter gradients. Also require strict checkpoint loading and a train/update/reload/inference smoke. Operator parity alone is insufficient.

Extend hosted CI across recorded Linux, Windows and macOS configurations. Run offline checks and substantive failure-path tests; add synthetic CPU model execution only where the required pinned dependencies install successfully. Test failed preflight without installation, unsupported targets, hash mismatches, unsafe build directories, subprocess failures and retained diagnostics. Publish model-execution claims only for configurations that actually pass. If source review establishes a CPU integration obstacle, document the anchored reason for deferral and retain the narrower CUDA scope.

Review affected setup lessons and references, preserve pending course reviews and the separate video escalation, and publish no raw data or weights. The source gaps below still prevent settling the CPU deliverable and exact CUDA patch contract.
